messages:
aj: FYI seeing a spike in RDMA handshake timeouts and packet retransmits from the eu-central dedicated GPU pool since the CNI rollout at ~08:22 UTC. Jobs hitting `rdma: transport timeout` and training throughput down ~25% :thinking_face:

maria: ugh. which CNI version rolled?

aj: cilium 1.25.2 -> 1.26.0 on the eu-central clusters. Canary looked fine but wide rollout started this morning.

kevin: any MTU errors in dmesg or `ip -s link`? RDMA is sensitive to fragmentation.

aj: grabbing a few outputs from a failing node: 
```\n# ip -d link show vxlan0
8: vxlan0@NONE: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> mtu 1450 qdisc noop state DOWN mode DEFAULT group default \n    vxlan id 42 remote 10.0.0.1 srcport 0 dstport 4789 nolearning aging 300
# ethtool -k eth0 | head -n 10
rx-checksumming: on\nlarge-receive-offload: off\n```

kevin: mtu 1450 is lower than the host's `--node-mtu` (we set 1500 previously). That difference could trigger fragmentation on encap paths. Which encap mode is in use?

aj: calico/cilium config shows `enableEncap: true` (vxlan) for most nodes, but a subset was auto-configured to `geneve` during the rollout due to kernel capability probe. Suspect mixed encap in same AZ pair.

henry: mixed encap across nodes = asymmetry. Some pods try to reach via vxlan (1450) while the other side expects geneve (default 1472), leads to fragmentation or drops under RDMA handshake size.

ingrid: spotted broken PMTU discovery logs on a test pod: `ICMP frag needed, but DF set` from node-b -> node-c. That's classic path MTU mismatch.

sre-bot: alert: Dedicated-eu-central GPU pool health degraded (latency P99 ↑, packet drop ↑). Auto-scaling paused for impacted AZs.

maria: can we confirm if `ip_nonlocal_bind` or `rp_filter` changed? and whether host MTU was changed by an image config?

aj: checked cloud-init logs — no host MTU changes. But the cilium datapath probe toggles off GRO/LRO on some NICs during install. I saw `gro: off` on west-facing interfaces.

kevin: toggle off GRO/LRO can increase CPU and fragment behavior for small packets; combined with MTU mismatch and encap mix, RDMA pops.

henry: quick experiment: on a failing node, change the pod's host-facing interface to force consistent encap and bump MTU to 1472. Test pod then completed handshake twice in a row.

aj: patch plan: 1) pause rollout in eu-central (done), 2) roll back to cilium 1.25.2 on impacted AZs, 3) run MTU/encap consistency probe across nodes, 4) reconcile dataplane GRO/LRO settings.

ingrid: +1. I'll run a k8s job that probes all node pairs with `ping -M do -s 1400` and a small RDMA handshake tool to validate.

maria: also add a temporary routing rule to force same-encap path while we validate (force vxlan on the odd nodes).

aj: logs attached inline: `kubectl logs -n rdma-training rdma-client-5` shows repeated `rdma: QP wait for conn timed out` and `RC: RETRY_EXCEEDED` errors.

kevin: let's not forget to calculate cost impact — failed runs are burning reserved slots. Henry, can you estimate % capacity loss so finance can be notified?

henry: preliminary estimate: eu-central ded pool throughput dropped 23% since 08:30 UTC, roughly ~14 GPU-hours wasted so far. I'll update the dashboard and ping finance.

maria: after rollback we'll redeploy canary with explicit `encap: vxlan` and `node-mtu: 1472` and keep a 30-min observation window. If stable, proceed rolling upgrade with the datapath fix.

aj: rolling back now for the impacted AZs. I'll update thread with probe results (ingrid, henry watching). :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: incident ticket #INC-2026-455 created, severity: medium, owner: aj.

kevin: thanks everyone. After this we should add an automated encap+mtu consistency check as a preflight for CNI rollouts.

aj: agreed — creating a PR for the rollout checklist after we close the incident.
